statement.p:
We are making 9-letter words from the set of letters a,b,c,d,e,f \dots, in such a way that we have exactly the first 9 letters available so that we use all letters.
How many 9-letter words can we make from the letters without repeats that do not contain the sub-word bad in consecutive letters?

li.p: How many words dont contain the subword bad in not-necessarily-consecutive letters (but in order)?

solution.p: There are 7 spots to start the word, and then there are 6! ways to arrange the other letters in the remaining three spots. Thus the number of words avoiding the sub-word bad in consecutive letters is 9! - 7\cdot 6!={357840}\text{.}

If we now need to avoid words that put b before a before d, we must choose which spots those letters go (in that order) and then arrange the remaining 6 letters. Thus, 9! - {9 \choose 3}6!={302400} words.
